note: Quick, Draw! vase 5214372580294656 (Thailand). Stroke 0 is the mouth, an oval at the top. Stroke 1 is the left side: down the neck, out over the shoulder and down the round body to the foot. Stroke 2 is a short tick at the bottom of the foot. Stroke 3 is the right side drawn upward from the foot: along the base, up the body, in over the shoulder and up the neck to the mouth. The film's pot is a wide painted bowl that a hand turns about its upright axis while the camera holds still; its outline does not change, so the rig holds the whole doodle rigid, placed by two points (the centre of the mouth and the centre of the foot) at one size for the whole shot. What moves in the film is the painted pattern sliding to the right across the body as the pot turns; that is drawn as extra marks (shots/vase/drawn) that travel round the body on a cylinder, narrowing as they reach the edge. A vase has no facing; facing is set to -1 only so that the rig, whose facing test compares the mouth and foot x, never mirrors the doodle.
